items.title: 5 Consumer Staples Stocks Reaching New Highs as Markets Retreat
items.summary: Here are five consumer staples stocks reaching fresh 52-week highs as investors seek defensive safety and reliable dividends amid the broader market selloff.

items.title: What Does Warren Buffett’s 90/10 Rule Say to a 74-Year-Old With $1 Million of Coca-Cola at a Record?
items.summary: Coca-Cola sits at an all-time high, and one couple's biggest holding now dwarfs the simple split Buffett prescribed for retirees. Getting there means choosing among five paths, and each one sends the IRS a different bill.

items.title: Unusual Call Option Activity in Coca-Cola - Is KO Stock Undervalued or Overvalued?
items.summary: Today, short-dated Coca-Cola call options are unusually active. Does this mean KO is undervalued, or are investors flocking to consumer staple stocks like KO to avoid all the tech drama?

items.title: PepsiCo Stock Drops 2.4% in 6 Months: Is More Downside Ahead?
items.summary: PEP's shares decline as weak North American demand, rising costs and lowered earnings guidance cloud its near-term recovery prospects.

items.title: Coca-Cola Has Crushed PepsiCo in 2026, but Retirement Investors Face a Different Dividend Decision
items.summary: One Dividend King trades at a steep premium while the other offers a yield above 4%. For retirees who need income to last decades, the cheaper stock may hide the bigger problem, and the pricier one may hide a surprising weak spot.

items.title: WisdomTree U.S. Dividend Growth (DGRW) Adds Microsoft and Nvidia on Nov. 12
items.summary: The fund bought $586.1 million of stock and sold nothing, lifting 184 positions.

items.title: Forget Nvidia: One Investor Says “the Bubble Is in Consumer Staple Stocks” Like Coca-Cola
items.summary: Key TakeawaysCoca-Cola closed at a record high on Nov. 13, the day after Nvidia announced its CEO’s resignation, and it trades at 29x forward earnings, the top of its 10-year range.

items.title: A Stock That Has Raised Its Dividend Every Year Since 1963 Just Hit a Record High. It Handed a Couple Living on the Checks a $67,000 Reason Not to Sell
items.summary: A beverage maker that has raised its dividend every year since 1963 closed Friday at a record high. For a retired couple living on 20,000 of its shares, Social Security and a cash reserve, the federal income tax bill is $0. Here is why selling a quarter of the position at the top would cost about $67,000.
